title: Should home gym owners invest in machines?
summary: Advice for home gym owners considering machines: pick multipurpose ones, avoid internally weight-stacked cable stations that are heavy to move and need disassembly, prefer plate-loaded machines that resell for 70-80% of cost, only buy what you'll use at least weekly, and measure your space carefully.

claims.claim: If you buy a machine, make sure it serves several purposes (e.g. a cable machine usable for rows, triceps extensions and more), since you can't fit a machine per body part unless you have huge space.
Internally weight-stacked cable stations are horrendous for home gym owners: very heavy to move, often must be disassembled to move without breaking, and are a headache to reassemble or sell.
Always choose plate-loaded machines and cable stations: easier to move and in demand on the resale market.
With patience you can recover 70-80% of the initial investment when reselling plate-loaded equipment even after three or four years.
As a barbell purist he doesn't think guided plate-loaded machines (Hammer Strength style) are needed since most of their exercises can be done with a barbell.
He bought a preacher curl bench because he loves training biceps, and a hyperextension bench because lower back training prevents injuries.
Golden rule of the home gym: only buy equipment you will use at least once a week; otherwise it's wasted money.
Measure dimensions meticulously: in a tight garage a few inches can make or break a piece of equipment.
